rubric: eval/baseline.md — rel: actually evidence for this specific claim · marg: right topic, does not evidence the claim as phrased · irr: not about this claim at all
note: Verdicts are in RANK ORDER, index 0 = the source shown first. Joined to the report by claim text prefix, never by position — see eval/scripts/paths.mjs for what a positional join costs. Labels for 01-C1..C3 and 01-C5 agree source-for-source with eval/baseline.md's counts on the earlier run, which is the only external check available that this labelling pass is calibrated the same way.

claims.claim: The American Academy of Pediatrics recommended in 2014
claims.note: Only the MMWR prevalence paper evidences the 'majority still begin before 8:30' half. Ranks 6-8 are 1910/1911/1979 papers about high schools generally — the query's own words, a century out.

claims.claim: Teenagers require between eight and ten hours of sleep
claims.note: Nothing retrieved reports the 70%-get-under-seven prevalence the claim actually makes. The one rel is the closest thing to it.

claims.claim: The consequence is not subtle: pushing start times later
claims.note: The one genuinely good retrieval in the set, and it was good in the baseline too.

claims.claim: Studies show that this sleep debt is the primary driver
claims.note: Labelled rel for the substance, following eval/baseline.md's convention on this claim. Strictly, nothing evidences PRIMACY — 'the primary driver' is the part no paper here establishes, and the critique is what caught that.

claims.claim: If schools do not act, depression rates among teenagers will double
claims.note: 0 rel, and correctly so: an unfalsifiable prediction. No literature can support it as phrased.

claims.claim: A randomized controlled trial at a Chinese travel agency
claims.note: Rank 1 is the Ctrip trial registration — the paper the claim is about, and the one queryVariants.ts was built to reach. Rank 7 is the later Trip.com hybrid experiment: a different study, so marg.

claims.claim: Meanwhile, commercial office vacancy rates in major American cities
claims.note: Both rel are post-2020; the irrelevant ones are pre-2020 vacancy-rate papers matching on the words rather than the period the claim is about.

claims.claim: Research suggests that fully remote workers are less likely to be promoted
claims.note: 0 rel. The 'visibility' sense collapse the rerun named: tabletop gestures, supply chains, and global eye health.

claims.claim: Johannes Gutenberg introduced movable-type printing to Europe
claims.note: Wikipedia at rank 1 counts as rel for a general historical claim — it evidences the date. Its venue tier says what it is worth citing.

claims.claim: Movable type had already existed in Korea and China
claims.note: The best-retrieving claim after 01-C3. Rank 8 is 'DNA could have existed long before life itself' — 'existed ... before'.

claims.claim: The Protestant Reformation depended on cheap pamphlets
claims.note: Both rel speak to the witch-hunting half. NOTHING retrieved evidences the Reformation half — the claim has two limbs and the search only ever answered one.

claims.claim: Cities that adopted printing early experienced faster economic growth
claims.note: Rank 1 is Dittmar 2011, exactly the paper. Ranks 2-8 are seven papers about cities, or growth, or printing, and none about all three.

claims.claim: What distinguished the European case was the alphabet's small character set
claims.note: 0 rel. A three-limbed claim; 'The Merchant as Character on Paper' is the merchant+paper+character collapse from the rerun.
